headers.comment: Default: never cache. Every path here serves index.html via the SPA rewrite, and index.html points at the fingerprinted assets — so caching it serves a stale app after a deploy (Firebase's own default is max-age=3600). Matching '**' rather than '/index.html' because the rewritten routes ('/', '/settings', ...) are what browsers actually request. When several header rules match, Firebase applies the LAST one, so this general rule must come before the asset rule below.
Vite fingerprints these, so a new build is always a new URL and they can be cached forever.
